title: Extreme direction Sperner for square 0-1 matrix

statement.text: Let ''A'' be an <math>n \times n</math> 0-1 matrix, and suppose that the facets of the polyhedron <math>P=\{x: A x \leq {\mathbf 1},\ x \leq {\mathbf 1}\} </math> are coloured by <math>n</math> colours such that a facet with extreme direction <math>-e_i</math> does not get colour <math>i</math>, and every colour appears twice. Can we find in polynomial time a vertex that is incident to facets of every colour (a ''panchromatic vertex'')?

status_observation.evidence: pinned EGRES Open MediaWiki revision and categories
